chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sayrafi, from Mufazzal ibn Qays ibn Rummana, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and mentioned to him some of my state. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O maid! Bring that bag! These are four hundred dinars which Abu Ja'far sent to me, so take them and ease (your financial problems) with them.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I said, 'No, by Allah! May I be sacrificed for you! This is not my purpose, but I would love it if you could supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I shall be doing it, but beware of informing the people with all of your state, for you would be belittled by them.'

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (expression of devotion)

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Sadiq give regarding revealing one's personal state to others?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the nuanced Shia perspective on dignity (*karam*) and the strategic concealment of need (*istikhfa’*) even when receiving substantial wealth from the Caliphate. Imam al-Sadiq’s advice to Mufazzl ibn Qays highlights that publicizing one's poverty can diminish one's social standing and spiritual worth, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on maintaining self-respect while relying on divine provision.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir, from Muhammad Bin Ibrahim Al Sayrafi, from Mufazzal Bin Qays Bin Rummana who said,

‘I came over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I mentioned to him some of my state. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O maid! Bring me<sup>asws</sup> that bag!’ These are the four hundred Dinars which were sent to me by Abu Ja’far (Al-Mansour the Caliph), so take these and ease (your financial problems) with these’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! This is not my purpose, but I would love it if you<sup>asws</sup> could supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> shall be doing it, but beware of informing the people with all of your state, for you would be belittled by them’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad have narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan from al-‘Abbas ibn ‘Amir from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sayrafiy from Mufaddal ibn Qays ibn Rummanah who has said the following:

“Once I visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and mentioned to him certain matters about my conditions. The Imam asked the housemaid to bring to him a certain bag, then he said, ‘This is the four hundred dinar that abu Ja’far (the Abbaside rule) has sent to me as a gift. Take it to ease your difficulties.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I do not want to take the money; it is not everything in my life. I love most that you pray for me before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious.’ The Imam said, ‘I will certainly do so; however, you must never speak to people about your conditions; you will seem insignificant in their sight.’”
